articles.summary: In the one-year anniversary episode of Galaxy Grid, the hosts unpack a turbulent week for digital assets as Bitcoin posts its first red weekly close since September amid heavy ETF outflows. The panel breaks down the market's sudden wall of worry, analyzing whether OpenAI’s latest algorithmic math breakthroughs pose a legitimate existential threat to foundational cryptography, alongside the fallout from a third-party Ledger supply chain attack. The discussion then shifts to onchain market structure with a look at Paper Trade, a newly launched zero-slippage, 1000x leverage perps protocol on Hyper EVM, and how traders immediately exploited its underlying mechanics. Finally, Thad and Will present their latest quantitative research, detailing why broad-based tokenized stocks severely underperform in automated market makers (AMMs) and breaking down the harsh reality of retail profitability and algorithmic edge on Polymarket. articles.summary: In this episode of Galaxy Grid, the hosts break down a massive Q3 close for crypto, with Bitcoin trading above $80K and Ethereum posting its best quarter since Q3 2024. The panel unpacks the structural drivers behind the recent market resilience, including strong ETF inflows, rising onchain DEX volumes, and major tokenized equity announcements from ICE and OKX. The discussion also covers the potential launch of a Polymarket token, analyzing whether the leading prediction market actually needs one as a user acquisition tool. Finally, the hosts examine the fallout from the $387 million Bitget hack—the largest of the year—and explore the Ethereum Foundation's new ZK API initiative, which could lay the groundwork for a new era of onchain privacy and secure AI inference.
